{"id":"015c9ef4-ac30-768d-928b-847320902575","paper_group_id":"015c9ef4-ac30-768d-928b-847320902575","title":"Attention Is All You Need","abstract":"The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or
convolutional neural networks in an encoder-decoder configuration. The best
performing models also connect the encoder and decoder through an attention
mechanism. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based
solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions
entirely. Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models to be
superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly
less time to train. Our model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014
English-to-German translation task, improving over the existing best results,
including ensembles by over 2 BLEU. On the WMT 2014 English-to-French
translation task, our model establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art
BLEU score of 41.8 after training for 3.5 days on eight GPUs, a small fraction
of the training costs of the best models from the literature. We show that the
Transformer generalizes well to other tasks by applying it successfully to
English constituency parsing both with large and limited training data.","feed_description":"Attention-based sequence models eliminate recurrence, enabling more parallelizable training while capturing long-range dependencies for translation and parsing.","pdf_only":false,"paper_summary":{"summary":"The paper presents the Transformer, a machine-translation system that lets tokens exchange context directly through multi-head self-attention instead of passing information sequentially. Its decoder trains in parallel with masking but generates translations autoregressively. On WMT 2014 English-to-German, Transformer big reaches 28.4 BLEU versus 26.36 for ConvS2S Ensemble, with lower estimated training FLOPs; this does not show every Transformer is cheaper.","feedDescription":"Attention-based sequence models eliminate recurrence, enabling more parallelizable training while capturing long-range dependencies for translation and parsing.","originalProblem":["Existing sequence transduction models (RNNs/LSTMs) suffered from slow training due to their inherent sequential computation, limiting parallelization.","Learning long-range dependencies in sequences was challenging for RNNs and CNNs due to increasing path lengths for information flow.","The computational cost and training time for achieving state-of-the-art results in tasks like machine translation were high, often requiring complex ensemble models."],"solution":["Introduces the Transformer, an encoder-decoder architecture that entirely eschews recurrence and convolutions, relying solely on self-attention mechanisms.","Utilizes Multi-Head Attention, which projects queries, keys, and values into multiple subspaces to allow the model to attend to different aspects of the input simultaneously.","Incorporates positional encodings to inject information about the relative or absolute position of tokens, as the attention mechanism itself lacks sequential awareness."],"keyInsights":["Replacing recurrence and convolutions with self-attention enables unprecedented parallelization, drastically reducing training times for sequence models.","Multi-head attention allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces, capturing diverse relational patterns.","Direct connections between any two positions via self-attention inherently improve the handling of long-range dependencies compared to RNNs or CNNs."],"results":["The Transformer (big) achieved a new state-of-the-art BLEU score of 28.4 on WMT 2014 English-to-German, a 2.0+ point improvement over previous SOTA ensemble models.","It significantly reduced training costs, achieving SOTA on English-to-French at less than 1/4 of the training cost of the previous best model.","The model demonstrated strong generalization by achieving 91.3 F1 on English constituency parsing (WSJ-only) with minimal task-specific tuning, outperforming several discriminative parsing
